Nutritional Implications Treatment goals and lifestyle 
changes that the patient is willing and able to make, rather than 
predetermined energy levels and percentages of carbohydrate,
protein, and fat, should be paramount in determining the
nutrition prescription. Th e aim of nutrition intervention is to 
support and facilitate lifestyle and behavior modiﬁ cations that
will result in improved metabolic control.23
Nutrition Diagnosis Common nutrition diagnoses 
associated with T2DM include excessive energy intake;
inadequate ﬂ uid intake (especially for HHS); excessive fat
intake; inappropriate intake of fats or carbohydrates; incon-
sistent carbohydrate intake; inadequate ﬁ ber intake; altered
GI function (gastroparesis); altered nutrition-related labora-
tory values; food-medication interaction; overweight/obesity 
(T2DM); food and nutrition-related knowledge deﬁ cit; harm-
ful beliefs/attitudes about food or nutrition-related topics; 
not ready for diet/lifestyle change; self-monitoring deﬁ cit;
